name: activity-tree-intent-geometry
description: A 200-character intent cannot starve a short delegate name or hide its own Open control. Real phone Sheet insets at the issue's 320/360/390/430px viewports through nine nested groups, a wide 900px row whose full name and 60% meta cap must be untouched, and Latin, full-width CJK and emoji labels plus an `xl` font-scale row, because the name floor is a text-relative budget rather than a digit measurement. Every row is measured twice in the same run, with the floor on and off, so the rows the floor did not rescue are proved unmoved.

mutation.declaration: activitypanel.module.css: remove .denseMeta's flex-shrink: 100 (the width reclamation's companion, .indentGuide's min() step cap, is recorded separately below)
mutation.note: Chrome exited 1 with flex-shrink: 100 removed and .denseMeta back to flex: 0 1 auto: 320px/depth 0 fell to 5.70px against its 12.58px glyph-plus-ellipsis prefix with 162px free, 320px/depth 1 to 5.17px against 12.58px, and 320px/depth 0 CJK to 3.61px against 22.80px. Proportional shrinking is what starves the name; the shrink weight is what makes the intent yield first. Stylesheet restored byte-for-byte before the passing run.

companion.declaration: activitypanel.module.css: revert .indentGuide's margin-left to the fixed calc(var(--space-3) + 6px)
companion.note: Chrome exited 1 with the indent step fixed at 18px again and flex-shrink: 100 kept: 320px/depth 8 CJK fell to 10.00px against its 22.80px prefix with 10px of room, 320px/depth 8 to 10.00px against 12.58px, and 320px/depth 9 to 0.00px against 12.58px with -9px, i.e. no room at all. A fixed step compounds 18px per level, so nine levels exceeded the 288px pane. Stylesheet restored byte-for-byte before the passing run.

previous.note: Chrome exited 1 on the restored pre-floor baseline of this same case: 320px/depth 1 dropped the name to 5.03px, 320px/depth 0 to 5.70px, 360px/depth 3 to 5.11px, 390px/depth 8 to 2.81px and 430px/depth 8 to 4.23px - all under the guard's 16px readable floor. The 430px root and the 900px row kept their full names (45.23px) in both runs, which is the comfortable-width half of the contract. Stylesheet restored byte-for-byte before the passing run.

Chrome exited 1: all nine names fell below 16px (6.84-9.61px) and every meta exceeded 60% of row content width. The 430px root also lost its full name. Stylesheet restored byte-for-byte before the passing runs.
